answer: Unique-anchor binding stops sybils: each identity must bind to one distinct, publicly verifiable anchor outside the chain, such as a separate domain or credential, that can anchor only one PoA identity per epoch. Like a ridge crossed at one pass per traveller, the same anchor cannot mint a second voice, and an orchard of fakes grown from one anchor is rejected at registration. An honest user binds one anchor cheaply, while an attacker wanting a thousand voices must acquire and maintain a thousand distinct anchors, paying registration per identity, a cost that grows with the ocean of fakes.
